description: The pistol squat is an advanced single-leg squat with one leg extended in front. It develops extreme unilateral quad and glute strength, balance, and mobility simultaneously.
tips: Stand on one leg with the other extended forward. Extend your arms forward for balance. Sit back and down on the standing leg, lowering all the way until your glute nearly touches your heel. Keep your extended leg parallel to the floor. Drive through your heel to stand back up. Repeat for desired reps then switch legs.

description: The box squat uses a box or bench as a depth target and briefly breaks momentum at the bottom. It develops quad and glute strength with consistent depth and reduced spinal stress.
tips: Set a box or bench to the desired depth behind you. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and toes slightly out. Sit back onto the box in a controlled manner, shifting weight to your heels. Pause briefly on the box. Drive explosively through your heels to stand. Repeat for desired reps.

description: The Bulgarian split squat is a single-leg squat with the rear foot elevated. It develops unilateral quad, glute, and hip flexor strength while exposing and correcting imbalances between sides.
tips: Stand in front of a bench and place one foot on top behind you. Hop the front foot forward enough to create a 90-degree knee angle at the bottom. Lower your hips until the front thigh is parallel to the floor and the back knee nearly touches the ground. Drive through the front heel to stand. Complete reps then switch legs.

description: Sentadilla de movilidad con un palo sostenido sobre la cabeza. Expone las limitaciones de tobillo, cadera y hombro sin cargar peso, y sirve para pulir el patrón antes de cargar.
tips: Sujeta el palo con agarre amplio y llévalo sobre la cabeza con los codos extendidos. Baja tan profundo como puedas manteniendo el palo alineado sobre el centro del pie y el pecho alto. Sube sin dejar que el palo se vaya adelante.
commonMistakes: Dejar que el palo caiga hacia delante; levantar los talones; juntar las rodillas al subir; buscar profundidad redondeando la espalda baja.

description: The squat jump is a plyometric exercise that develops explosive lower body power by combining a squat with a maximal vertical jump. It trains fast-twitch muscle fibers in the quads and glutes.
tips: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and toes slightly out. Lower into a squat until thighs are parallel to the floor. Explosively jump as high as possible by extending your hips, knees, and ankles simultaneously. Land softly on the balls of your feet with knees slightly bent. Immediately descend into the next squat. Repeat for desired reps.

description: The Smith machine squat uses a guided barbell on fixed vertical rails, providing additional stability. It allows focus on leg drive without balance demands of a free barbell.
tips: Position yourself under the Smith machine bar with it resting on your upper back. Set your feet slightly in front of you. Unhook the bar by rotating it. Descend by bending your knees and pushing them out over your toes. Lower until thighs are parallel. Drive up to standing. Re-rack by rotating the bar back into the hooks. Repeat for desired reps.

description: The front squat holds the barbell in front of the body across the shoulders, increasing quad dominance and requiring greater core strength and upper back mobility than the back squat.
tips: Hold the barbell in a front rack position across your front deltoids. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and toes slightly out. Keep your elbows high and chest up. Sit down and forward until thighs are parallel to the floor. Drive through your feet to stand. Repeat for desired reps.

description: The goblet squat holds a dumbbell or kettlebell at chest height, acting as a counterbalance to maintain an upright torso. It is excellent for learning squat mechanics.
tips: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell vertically at your chest with both hands. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and toes slightly out. Push your knees out and squat down until thighs are parallel or below parallel to the floor. Drive through your heels to stand. Repeat for desired reps.

description: The hack squat machine places the body at an angle on a platform, providing a guided squat path that emphasizes the quads with reduced lower back stress.
tips: Load the hack squat machine and position yourself with your back flat against the pad and shoulders under the pads. Feet on the platform slightly wider than shoulder-width. Release the safety. Lower by bending your knees until thighs are parallel to the platform. Drive through your feet to press back up. Repeat for desired reps.

description: The sumo squat uses a wide stance with toes pointed out to shift emphasis toward the inner thighs (adductors) and glutes compared to a standard squat. Can be performed with a dumbbell or kettlebell.
tips: Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width and toes pointed out at 45 degrees. Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell in front of you. Push your knees out over your toes and lower your hips until thighs are parallel to the floor. Drive through your heels to stand back up. Squeeze your glutes at the top. Repeat for desired reps.

description: The barbell back squat is the king of lower body exercises, targeting the quads, glutes, hamstrings, and core under heavy load. It is the most effective compound movement for lower body mass.
tips: Place a barbell on your upper back and stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width, toes pointed slightly out. Take a deep breath and brace your core. Push your knees out over your toes and sit your hips back and down until thighs are parallel to the floor. Drive through your heels to stand. Repeat for desired reps.

description: The step-up is a unilateral leg exercise using a box or bench that targets the quads and glutes. It develops single-leg strength and balance in a functional movement pattern.
tips: Stand in front of a box or bench. Step up with one foot and drive through that heel to lift your body onto the box. Stand fully upright on top. Step back down with the trailing foot. Repeat on the same leg or alternate. Complete desired reps.

description: The superman hold is a bodyweight lower back and glute exercise performed lying face down. Lifting the arms and legs simultaneously activates the entire posterior chain with minimal equipment.
tips: Lie face down on a mat with arms extended overhead and legs straight. Simultaneously raise your arms, chest, and legs off the floor by squeezing your glutes and lower back. Hold the top position for 2-3 seconds. Lower back down with control. Repeat for desired reps.

description: The kettlebell swing is a fundamental hip hinge movement that develops explosive hip extension, posterior chain strength, and cardiovascular conditioning. It uses the power of the hips rather than the arms.
tips: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and a kettlebell on the floor slightly in front of you. Hinge at the hips and grip the bell. Pull it back between your legs with a hiking motion. Drive your hips forward explosively to swing the bell to chest height. Let gravity bring it back through your legs and immediately repeat. Use your hips not your arms.

description: The Prone Y-T-W is a floor-based rear delt and lower trapezius exercise performed lying face down. It targets the muscles most commonly weakened by desk posture and excessive pressing: posterior deltoids, lower trapezius, and rhomboids.
tips: Lie face down on the floor with arms extended. For Y: raise arms at 45° angle above head, thumbs up. Hold 2 sec. For T: raise arms straight out to the sides. Hold 2 sec. For W: bend elbows to 90° and raise them like goal posts. Hold 2 sec. Lower between each letter. Perform 2-3 sets of 8-10 reps per letter.
commonMistakes: Move slowly and with control. Thumbs point up throughout. Keep the neck neutral — do not crane it upward. Each letter is a distinct position held for 2 seconds.

description: The lunge is a fundamental unilateral lower body exercise targeting the quads, glutes, and hamstrings. It also challenges balance and hip mobility in a split stance position.
tips: Stand with feet hip-width apart. Step forward with one foot and lower your body until both knees are bent at about 90 degrees. Keep your front knee over your foot and back knee just above the floor. Push through your front heel to return to the starting position. Repeat on the same leg or alternate legs for desired reps.

description: The walking lunge is a dynamic lunge variation where you move continuously forward, increasing time under tension and cardiovascular demand compared to stationary lunges.
tips: Stand with feet hip-width apart. Step forward with one foot into a lunge, lowering until both knees are at 90 degrees. Drive through the front foot to step forward into the next lunge with the opposite leg. Continue walking forward for the desired distance or reps. Maintain upright posture throughout.

description: The reverse lunge steps backward instead of forward, reducing knee stress compared to the forward lunge. It emphasizes glute and hamstring activation while maintaining stability.
tips: Stand with feet hip-width apart. Step one foot back and lower your back knee toward the floor until both knees are at 90 degrees. Keep your front knee over your ankle. Push through your front heel to return to standing. Alternate legs or complete all reps on one side. Repeat for desired reps.
